Runway has shortened every month, from {{fact:4e6971f5-1058-4866-a2e0-af324ac4d0dc}} months at July 31 to {{fact:9cb8edab-f0ed-47d3-a593-3052389e5299}} months at October 31. This points to sustained cash burn without fresh funding. It is the likely driver of the two covenant headroom signals, which show the same erosion against the runway and cash tests.

This is the covenant view of the falling runway. Headroom has narrowed from {{fact:9e7601bb-0498-468a-bf82-c27e0f0ca1ac}} in August to {{fact:988eb01a-2ade-4939-b5a5-ae4ec33ab4dc}} in October, with runway at {{fact:03b5274b-ce22-44dc-a909-68cd4fb0797c}} months against a floor of {{fact:a3016cc7-c315-47bb-bba2-6eae70f903b9}}. It is still comfortably compliant, but the steady monthly decline matters if burn continues.

Unrestricted cash of {{fact:f294dc87-0da8-4b48-a408-60e6282f193e}} still clears the {{fact:c2893b24-aaa2-48eb-b939-7efd5860a9b2}} minimum. It reflects the same cash burn behind the shrinking runway and may be the first test to tighten.

The Revenue to Plan test fails for the three months ended October 31, 2026. Revenue was {{fact:2737650c-8e79-4228-994a-c72cc9df0fe9}} of the Approved Plan. Section 6.3 requires at least {{fact:b2d054c9-bf21-4d60-b8a2-a7ec5a3a8919}}. I reran the test under terms version 1, the only version on file, and it still fails, with headroom of {{fact:f28d0c06-d90c-4b24-a3b7-d3e43751dc72}}. The borrower's October certificate reports the same ratio, {{fact:8204fb36-f1b7-4530-8172-d344c070b721}}, and says the borrower is not in compliance. No unapproved amendments are on file. A search of the documents found no waiver and no written update to the Approved Plan. The test has no add-backs, so there is no cap to correct. The September certificate also reported this covenant out of compliance. This looks like a true breach. How to respond is for the credit team to decide.

Revenue reached {{fact:e959bfd5-abb7-47e5-a334-99dfbb8654e2}} of plan against a covenant floor of {{fact:3755719f-7547-4045-a3fd-6739b19e4094}}, so headroom is negative at {{fact:1fe991a3-04a0-442a-b354-f9570c0a7fb5}}. The covenant measure therefore sits below its threshold, not merely close to it. This is the covenant view of the same shortfall flagged by the revenue-below-plan signal.

Revenue came in at {{fact:a0ab2814-6e71-4861-8936-838587855357}} of plan, a material miss for a subscription business whose plan underpins its cash runway. It is the operating cause behind the revenue covenant falling below its floor. If the miss persists, it may also explain the steady erosion in cash headroom.

Unrestricted cash of {{fact:f6e501ae-5be2-4942-95b6-ecc0bf3ee257}} remains well above the {{fact:cf41bfe4-6836-4f51-aabf-2439f8c303cc}} minimum, but headroom has declined each month, from {{fact:b08244fb-64ac-46cf-989e-ab5bd9ef506f}} in August to {{fact:f08fbe81-7679-4c37-83bb-5be89804ee94}} in September and {{fact:808ba721-2a2c-424f-987c-32d347db04d9}} in October. Ongoing burn alongside the revenue shortfall would fit this pattern; liquidity is not yet tight.

Revenue covenant headroom has deteriorated each month, from {{fact:77903ce4-ac26-4ad9-8797-33d708ef5b43}} in August to {{fact:bd775118-40c4-46b5-873b-efe55abc61ae}} in September and {{fact:1fe991a3-04a0-442a-b354-f9570c0a7fb5}} in October. It turned negative in September and the gap widened in October, showing the shortfall is worsening rather than a one-month miss.
